### 1 — Scene
A toasted sandwich, apparently with egg and possibly cheese, alongside a fresh rice-paper vegetable roll and a small cup of dark dipping sauce. The glass appears to contain water.

### 2 — Vessel
A round disposable dinner plate, approximately **26 cm** across.
Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ **531 cm²**.

### 3–7 — Items, area, volume, weight, and energy
The filling and roll contents are partly obscured, so their identification and energy densities are approximate.

| Item | Plate area covered | Area × height = gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated grams | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Toasted bread, two slices | 33% | 175 cm² × 1.6 cm = 280 ml | 0.30 | 84 g | 280 | 235 kcal |
| Egg/cheese-like sandwich filling | Within bread footprint* | 133 cm² × 0.4 cm = 53 ml | 0.95 | 50 g | 220 | 110 kcal |
| Fresh rice-paper vegetable roll | 14% | 74 cm² × 2.0 cm = 148 ml | 0.85 | 126 g | 110 | 139 kcal |
| Dark dipping sauce, separate cup | Outside plate | Approximately 20 cm² × 1 cm = 20 ml | 1.0 | 20 g | 60 | 12 kcal |

*The filling occupies approximately 25% of the plate area underneath the bread; it is not counted twice in the coverage total. The sandwich and roll together cover approximately **47% of the plate**, leaving about half bare. No separate quantity of cooking oil is visibly measurable; the toasted bread estimate allows for light added fat.*

### 8 — Sanity check
Approximately **280 g including sauce** and **500 kcal** is plausible for the visible sandwich and single fresh roll. Water is excluded from the food weight and contributes no energy. The main uncertainty is the sandwich filling and whether the roll contains anything beyond vegetables.
